title: Stationary tower cohomology under ringed-site local bounds
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and use module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ be a weak Serre subcategory: it is strictly full, contains zero, and is closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between its objects and under extensions. Write $D_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal O)$ for complexes whose every cohomology sheaf lies in $\mathcal S$, and $D^+_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal O)$ for its bounded-below part. Suppose there is a set $\mathcal V\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ such that every object has a covering by members of $\mathcal V$. For every $V\in\mathcal V$ suppose there are an integer $d_V$ and a cofinal collection of covering families $\{V_i\to V\}$ such that $H^p(V_i,F)=0$ for every $p>d_V$ and $F\in\mathcal S$. Cofinal means every covering has a refinement in the collection, and $H^p(V_i,F)$ is the right derived functor of sections. Use the resolution-derived inverse limit on strict inverse sequences, whose underlying object has the Roos triangle [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], [def-weil-derived-limit]. Let $(L_n,u_n:L_{n+1}\to L_n)_{n\geq0}$ be an inverse sequence in $D^+_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal O)$, realized by a strict tower of complexes. The lower bound may depend on $n$. Suppose for each $j\in\mathbf Z$ there is $n_j\geq0$ such that $H^j(u_n)$ is an isomorphism for all $n\geq n_j$. Then, for every $j$ and every $n\geq n_j$, the canonical projection induces an isomorphism
$$H^j(R\varprojlim_mL_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^j(L_n).$$
In particular $R\varprojlim_mL_m\in D_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal O)$.

source.place: Tag 0D6T, lemma-olsson-laszlo-modified, statement and proof, with its canonical projection maps; local bound hypotheses spelled out from situation-olsson-laszlo

proof.text: Put $L=R\varprojlim L_n$ with its specified projections. For any $E\in D(\mathcal O)$, take a K-injective representative $I$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and put $P_E^q(U)=H^q(\Gamma(U,I))$. Exact abelian sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] sends the sectionwise kernel/image quotient defining $P_E^q$ to the kernel/image quotient defining $H^q(E)$. Thus $(P_E^q)^\#=H^q(E)$ as underlying abelian sheaves. The module structure is the one on abelian sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. These identifications commute with restriction and with the induced maps of cohomology, since all maps are induced on the same kernels and quotients (using functorial resolutions before passing to the derived category).

source.place: Tag 0BKV, lemma-sheafification-cohomology, proof; the kernel/image calculation, also used twice in the proof of Tag 0D6T

proof.text: By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], the units in Step 1 also exhibit set sheafification. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local]: every section of $H^q(E)$ is locally represented by an element of $H^q(U,E)$, and a representative whose sheaf image is zero restricts to zero on a covering. We will use both assertions for $E=L$ and $E=L_N$. On an object $V\in\mathcal V$ these coverings, and any composite refinement used for zero detection, may be refined to a covering in the given cofinal collection. Representatives and equalities restrict along the refinement arrows.

source.place: Tag 0D6T, proof, uses of Tag 0BKV; Tag 0D6L, proof, local representatives and their refinement

proof.text: Fix $j$ and $V\in\mathcal V$, and replace $d_V$ by $d=\max(0,d_V)$, which preserves the assumed vanishing. Choose $N_0\geq n_j$ at least all the finitely many thresholds $n_q$ for $j-d-2\leq q\leq j+1$. For any $N\geq N_0$ and $m\geq N$, the composite $L_m\to L_N$ induces isomorphisms in that interval. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-bounded-below-section-window-comparison] with $a=j-1,b=j$ and $U=W$, separately for every member $W$ of every covering in the cofinal collection of $V$. Its bound holds for every sheaf in $\mathcal S$ by hypothesis; each $L_m,L_N$ is bounded below, with no bound uniform in $m$ needed. Hence the actual transition maps on both $H^{j-1}(W,L_m)$ and $H^j(W,L_m)$ are isomorphisms throughout the tail $m\geq N$. The same $N_0$ works for all these $W$.

source.place: Tag 0D6T, proof, first paragraph, displayed finite interval and comparison of spectral sequences

proof.text: For every such $W$, apply [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit] to the specified Roos triangle $L\xrightarrow{p}\prod^D_mL_m\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod^D_mL_m\to L[1]$ of the strict tower, which is distinguished by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] and hence a derived-limit triangle in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]; the canonical projections are $\operatorname{pr}_m\circ p$. It gives a Roos triangle for $R\Gamma(W,L)$ with the projections $R\Gamma(W,L)\to R\Gamma(W,L_m)$ induced by the original projections. Consecutive composites in the triangle vanish, so the induced cohomology maps form a compatible family. They therefore define a map $b:H^j(W,L)\to\varprojlim_m H^j(W,L_m)$ whose $m$th component is exactly the cohomology of the canonical projection.

source.place: Tag 0D6K, lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim; Tag 0D6T, proof, short exact sequence comparison

proof.text: The eventual isomorphisms in degree $j-1$ give $R^1\varprojlim_m H^{j-1}(W,L_m)=0$ by [lem-pc-derived-limit-eventually-iso]. Apply [lem-pc-milnor-boundary-factorization] to the triangle from Step 4: its exactness at $H^j(W,L)$, with zero left term, makes the map to the product of the $H^j(W,L_m)$ injective, and hence makes $b$ injective. Apply [lem-pc-milnor-projection-factorization] to this same $b$ and its component equations to obtain surjectivity. Projection from the inverse limit to level $N\geq N_0$ is bijective: a level-$N$ value determines the earlier values by forward transitions and the later values uniquely by the inverse tail isomorphisms. Thus the actual projection $H^j(W,L)\to H^j(W,L_N)$ is an isomorphism for every such $W$ and every $N\geq N_0$.

source.place: Tag 0D6T, proof, application of Tag 0D6K and eventual constancy; more-algebra.tex Tag 07KY, remark-compare-derived-limit

proof.text: Fix any $n\geq n_j$. To show injectivity of $\phi_n:H^j(L)\to H^j(L_n)$, take a kernel section on any object and cover that object by members $V\in\mathcal V$. Choose $N\geq\max(n,N_0(V))$. The sheaf map $H^j(L_N)\to H^j(L_n)$ is an isomorphism, so the section also has zero image at level $N$. By Step 2 represent it on a covering of $V$ by classes in $H^j(W,L)$; their level-$N$ images have zero sheaf image. Refine once more so those images vanish as derived section classes, then refine the composite covering to a member of the cofinal collection. On each final member $W$, Step 5 makes the projection to $H^j(W,L_N)$ injective, so the restricted representative is zero. Sheaf separatedness now kills the original kernel section. This proves injectivity on every object.

source.place: Tag 0D6T, proof, first paragraph, injectivity via Tag 0D6L; the local representative argument of Tag 0D6L is expanded here

proof.text: For surjectivity, start with $\gamma\in H^j(L_n)(U)$ and cover $U$ by objects $V\in\mathcal V$. Choose $N\geq\max(n,N_0(V))$ and use the inverse of $H^j(L_N)\to H^j(L_n)$ to lift $\gamma|_V$ to a sheaf section at level $N$. By Step 2, after a refinement in the cofinal collection, represent it by classes in $H^j(W,L_N)$. Step 5 lifts each such class to $H^j(W,L)$, whose sheaf image maps to $\gamma|_W$, by the naturality of Step 1 and compatibility of projections. Thus every target section lifts locally. Step 6 makes the local lifts agree after every common restriction, since their images agree; the sheaf axiom glues them uniquely. Hence $\phi_n$ is bijective on sections of every object, and its inverses are restriction-compatible and $\mathcal O$-linear. It is the required isomorphism of module sheaves. Finally $H^j(L_n)\in\mathcal S$ and strict fullness of $\mathcal S$ imply $H^j(L)\in\mathcal S$ for every $j$, proving $L\in D_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal O)$.

source.place: Tag 0D6T, proof, second paragraph, lifting a section on a cofinal covering and conclusion
